key_insight: Including solute transport and mass conservation changes predicted droplet impact and solidification behavior, because local composition alters mushy-zone thickness and thus the flow.
engineering_relevance: The model improves prediction of alloy splat formation and segregation defects, helping guide additive manufacturing and coating processes where cracking risk matters.
method: Fully coupled multiphysics model for multiphase hydrodynamics, wetting, conjugate heat transfer, phase change, and mass transfer.
Concentration-flux-correction algorithm to conserve solute mass at the discretization level.
Validated against several benchmarks before simulating alloy droplet impact and macrosegregation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports careful benchmark validation and shows better agreement with experiments when mass transfer and solute transport are included.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on resolving mushy-region physics and concentration transport; coarse grids or simplified solute models may miss segregation hotspots.
paper_title: Numerical Modeling of a Metallic Alloy Droplet Impact, Solidification, and Macrosegregation
